It already reads iPhone LiDAR RGB-D (Stray Scanner gives RGB video plus 256x192 depth, the same shape as our data), and its `-w` mode streams the growing map to a Spark web viewer. That is a ready template for 'splat builds while scanning, viewed in the browser'. We would write a reader for the LiteReality Scanner format, could feed ARKit poses as initialization to skip or ease tracking, and would run it on a Modal GPU fed by frames streamed from the phone. 2D surfels also give accurate geometry for the MuJoCo side. The unknown is speed, which is not reported.

all.name: GS-ICP SLAM (ECCV 2024, '100 FPS Gaussian Splatting SLAM')
all.what: RGB-D SLAM that tracks with G-ICP on Gaussian covariances (via fast_gicp) and maps with 3DGS in a separate thread that shares covariances. The paper reports up to 107 FPS, in a mode where tracking speed is unlimited.
all.license: MIT at the repo level. The bundled diff-gaussian-rasterization submodule is Inria-derived and non-commercial.

We already have ARKit poses, so we could drop G-ICP tracking and keep the mapping thread: new Gaussians are initialized straight from the LiDAR depth, which matches our 'instant' surfel splat, with continuous refinement. Quality is below offline training, so for rung 1 it serves as a fast seed, not the final splat.

all.name: Taming 3DGS (+ Speedy-Splat) as kernel/schedule donors for our gsplat trainer
all.what: Taming 3DGS provides budget-controlled densification (a predictable Gaussian count) and a fast per-splat-parallel backward pass with sparse Adam. Speedy-Splat provides precise tile intersection plus aggressive pruning (soft and hard) for much faster training and rendering. Both are components of the SIGGRAPH Asia 2025 winning pipeline.
all.license: Taming is MIT (LICENSE text read). Speedy-Splat carries the Inria Gaussian-Splatting license (non-commercial).
all.fit: Rung 1 speed and rung 3 frame rate. A Gaussian budget sized to the room keeps per-room training time and the Spark payload predictable, which matters for several viewers on a call. Pruning reduces the Gaussian count, which helps browser frame rate and stripping weak floaters. Because Taming is MIT, its ideas can go into our gsplat 1.5.3 code directly. Separately, gsplat main (not yet on PyPI) has 2026 kernel speedups for 3DGS/3DGUT rasterization, roughly 30% on some paths, plus native MCMC perturbation. Upgrading from 1.5.3 to main is a cheap win to measure first.
all.evidence: Checked with gh: taming-3dgs is MIT (license text read), 369 stars, last push 2025-06-16. speedy-splat is Inria Gaussian-Splatting license (text read), 361 stars, last push 2026-02-18. gsplat README: the 'Changes on main since v1.5.3' list includes Jun/Jul 2026 faster rasterization and kernels; the latest tagged release is v1.5.3 (2025-07-04). Speed multipliers are from paper claims and I did not re-verify them.

all.speed: Taming: minutes rather than tens of minutes for full 3DGS on benchmarks (paper). Speedy-Splat: about 6x faster training per its paper (not re-verified). Combined, they reached the 1-minute budget in the challenge.

all.name: DN-Splatter / AGS-Mesh (depth + normal supervised splatting for indoor phone captures)
all.what: A nerfstudio/gsplat method that adds sensor-depth and normal supervision, plus depth/normal filtering (AGS-Mesh), to Gaussian splatting for indoor scenes. It targets iPhone/Polycam/MuSHRoom-style LiDAR captures, with monocular-normal (DSINE/Omnidata) and patch-depth-correlation options and TSDF mesh export.
all.license: Apache-2.0 (gsplat-based, so no Inria rasterizer)
all.fit: Floater and geometry fix for rung 1, and geometric accuracy for rungs 1 and 2. It is the most license-clean reference for depth-supervised losses using iPhone LiDAR. We would port its depth loss, depth-gradient normal loss and LiDAR-confidence filtering into our gsplat trainer. The aim is to stop smeared floors and floaters in barely-seen views, keep geometry true for frame-by-frame comparison against the held-out phone clip, and get a mesh for MuJoCo. It is not fast by itself, since it is a nerfstudio training loop.

all.gpu: Fits on a 24 GB GPU
all.weights: Optional DSINE/Omnidata normal-estimator weights fetched by scripts

all.name: GPS-SLAM (Gaussian-plus-SDF SLAM, 150+ fps; successor of RTG-SLAM)
all.what: A C++/CUDA RGB-D SLAM that represents geometry with an SDF (InfiniTAM) and uses Gaussians only for appearance residuals. It claims about 50% fewer Gaussians and 75% fewer iterations, and over 150 fps on real Azure Kinect sequences (250+ on Replica) on an RTX 4090.
all.license: AGPL-3.0 (strong copyleft; using it in a network service obliges source release)
all.fit: Rung 3. This is the fastest open RGB-D Gaussian reconstruction I found, and the SDF gives free-space carving for nothing: Gaussians live only near the fused surface, so floaters can't form in carved free space. The SDF also suits MuJoCo collision geometry. The release is incomplete, with no online viewer and no multiprocess trainer, and it needs third-party libraries from Baidu/Google Drive. Treat it as a reference design, or an AGPL-isolated backend service on Modal, rather than code to embed.

Repo contains InfiniTAM, gsplat, slam_trainer.cpp and remote_viewer.cpp. The README's 2025-10-18 note says the online viewer and multithreading are not ready; tested on a Ryzen 9950X3D with an RTX 4090. Project page gapszju.github.io/GPS-SLAM links this repo and gives the 150 fps claim but no quality table. The RTG-SLAM repo (GPL-3.0) points to GPS-SLAM as its successor.

all.name: GSFusion (online RGB-D mapping: Gaussian splatting + TSDF fusion, RA-L 2024)
all.what: An online mapper that runs TSDF fusion alongside 3DGS. It uses a quadtree to place Gaussians only where image detail demands it, so it gets compact maps with depth-consistent placement. All reported results are from a single RTX 3060. C++ with LibTorch, plus a Dockerfile.

Like GPS-SLAM, the TSDF provides free-space carving, and the tight surface-based Gaussian placement is a robust way to build our 'instant' splat from LiDAR while scanning. It takes known poses, which suits our ARKit poses better than full SLAM does. It runs on a modest GPU, so on Modal an L40S or A100 is plenty. Quality is below offline-trained splats.

all.name: Spark 2.x (sparkjsdev/spark) with paged LoD (.RAD) and dynamic SplatMesh editing
all.what: MIT three.js Gaussian splat renderer, maintained by World Labs. It renders several splat objects with correct sorting and several viewpoints at once. Every splat can be transformed, recolored or displaced at runtime, and a GPU shader graph creates and edits splats. Spark 2.0 (full release April 2026) added a build-lod CLI that writes a .RAD LoD tree, which the browser streams in pages as the camera moves.

all.weights: none needed (renderer)
all.inputs: any .ply/.spz/.splat/.ksplat or .RAD file; nothing scan-specific
all.speed: real-time in the browser. LoD keeps large scenes interactive on phones and laptops (vendor claim; I did not benchmark it).

all.fit: We already use it as the viewer, so we keep it and upgrade to 2.4.0. Rung 2: load the moved object as its own SplatMesh and move it by changing its transform, with no retraining. Rung 3: run build-lod on Modal right after training and stream the .RAD file, so walking stays at 30 fps. Rung 4: multi-viewpoint rendering, and each client renders locally from one shared asset, so we only sync poses and object transforms over the call. Spark has no networking layer; we write that ourselves.

GS-Share, CrossGaussian and arXiv 2604.02851 are papers with no code, and 2604.02851 is single-client Unity. So the multi-user layer we build on Spark would be new.

all.what: A nerfstudio/gsplat plugin. It supervises splat training with sensor depth (iPhone LiDAR) plus normals, either from the rendered depth gradient or from monocular networks (Omnidata, DSINE). Reported to improve novel-view synthesis and meshes on smartphone indoor captures such as MuSHRoom. It also supports SparseGS depth-correlation loss and TSDF meshing.

all.name: AnySplat (feed-forward 3DGS from unconstrained views)
all.what: A transformer that predicts Gaussians, depth and camera poses for a set of images in one forward pass, using geometry priors from VGGT. The repo includes a Gradio demo that renders RGB and depth videos along interpolated paths.
all.license: MIT (code and HF weights). It trains with VGGT pseudo-labels, so check VGGT's own license if we ship VGGT.
all.weights: https://huggingface.co/lhjiang/anysplat (public, not gated, license:mit, about 7.8k downloads)
all.inputs: uncalibrated RGB images or a video; no poses or depth needed. Our ARKit poses would be ignored unless we modify it.
all.speed: one feed-forward pass, seconds-scale per the paper (I did not check the exact numbers). Training it needs 8 GPUs; we only need inference.
all.gpu: single large GPU for inference with many views (H100 fine)
all.fit: Rung 1 speed. On Modal it could replace or seed the roughly 80 s gsplat run: an instant splat from 60-300 frames, then a few hundred gsplat steps with LiDAR depth loss. We would need to align its predicted poses and scale to ARKit metric space, or inject ARKit poses. Feed-forward splats usually trail optimized ones on PSNR, so use it as the init, not the final result. Another research agent probably covers feed-forward models in more depth.

all.name: SAGA: Segment Any 3D Gaussians
all.what: Promptable 3D segmentation of a trained Gaussian scene. It distills SAM masks into per-Gaussian affinity features and segments in milliseconds once trained. Its output is the set of Gaussians that belong to an object.
all.license: Apache-2.0
all.weights: uses public SAM weights; no scene weights
all.inputs: a trained 3DGS scene plus its posed training images. It runs SAM on those images and then trains an affinity field per scene.
all.speed: millisecond-level segmentation after a per-scene feature-training pass (minutes)
all.gpu: single CUDA GPU
all.fit: Rung 2 (object moved). We split the room splat into object SplatMeshes, for example chairs matched to RoomPlan object boxes, and move them in Spark. RoomPlan 3D boxes could replace clicks as prompts. Without the affinity training, a cheaper first version is to cut Gaussians inside each RoomPlan box. SAGA is the upgrade for clean edges.

all.name: Inpaint360GS (WACV 2026): object-aware 3D inpainting for 360 Gaussian scenes
all.what: Removes one or more objects from a 3DGS scene and fills the hole. It segments objects, inpaints 2D color and depth with LaMa, then optimizes the Gaussians to stay consistent across views. Code and dataset were released 2026-01-19. It beats AuraFusion360 (CVPR'25), which in turn has no code: its repo holds only the project page.
all.license: Apache-2.0 (LaMa dependency also Apache-2.0)
all.weights: uses public LaMa and segmentation models; nothing gated
all.inputs: posed multi-view images with shared intrinsics (COLMAP-style) plus a trained 3DGS scene
all.speed: per-scene optimization (minutes). Not real-time; the authors list feed-forward inpainting as future work.
all.gpu: single CUDA GPU; --resolution flag to fit memory
all.fit: Rung 2. When an object is moved, the floor or wall behind its old spot is a hole the scan never saw. Run this offline on Modal once per object at capture time to bake a 'clean background' splat, then show object SplatMeshes on top in Spark. Too slow to run live; a precompute step only.

all.name: Brush (Rust/WebGPU Gaussian splat trainer and viewer)
all.what: A full 3DGS training and viewing engine on WebGPU (Burn). It runs on macOS, Windows, Linux, Android and in Chrome/Edge, with no CUDA. It trains from COLMAP or nerfstudio transforms.json with optional masks, and views and streams .ply files from a URL, including 4D delta-frame animations.
all.license: Apache-2.0
all.weights: none
all.inputs: posed images (COLMAP or nerfstudio format); optional masks
all.speed: interactive training with a live viewer. Slower than gsplat on CUDA; no official H100 numbers.
all.gpu: any WebGPU device
all.fit: Mostly something to learn from, with possible rung 3 use. We could export our ARKit capture as nerfstudio transforms.json so Brush trains a few hundred refine steps in the browser or on the phone after the instant splat arrives. That moves training cost off Modal and gives a live 'improving' view on the call. Its delta-frame 4D ply format is a ready transport for moved-object animations. Our Modal gsplat path stays the main pipeline.

all.name: Physics splats: PhysTwin (+ Boba), OmniPhysGS, PhysGaussian
all.what: PhysTwin builds a spring-mass plus Gaussian 'digital twin' of a deformable object from video and runs an interactive playground. Its 2026 follow-up Boba (ECCV'26) batches rollouts at about 3,310 FPS aggregate. OmniPhysGS (ICLR'25) and PhysGaussian (CVPR'24) run MPM simulation directly on the Gaussians.
all.license: PhysTwin MIT; OmniPhysGS MIT; PhysGaussian has NO license file (all rights reserved by default)
all.weights: PhysTwin ships processed data and pretrained cases; it depends on TRELLIS, Grounded-SAM-2 and SDXL for building new twins. The other two have no learned weights needed.
all.inputs: PhysTwin: multi-view RGB-D video of a hand interacting with the object (RealSense rigs), not a static phone room scan. OmniPhysGS and PhysGaussian: a trained object-level 3DGS plus material settings or prompts.
all.speed: PhysTwin playground about 37 FPS on an RTX 4090 with about 2-4 GB; first-order fit about 5 min, CMA-ES about 12 min. MPM methods are offline per clip.
all.gpu: single CUDA GPU
all.fit: Little direct use. Our physics is rigid furniture in MuJoCo, which is simpler and better matched. The usable idea for rungs 2 and 3 is the PhysTwin/Boba pattern of driving Gaussian positions from a simulator by linear blend skinning. Mirror that by binding each object's SplatMesh transform to its MuJoCo body pose every frame in Spark. Don't adopt the codebases.

all.name: nerfstudio splatfacto with Polycam/Record3D importers
all.what: The reference open pipeline from phone capture to splat. ns-process-data has polycam and record3d converters that keep ARKit poses and LiDAR depth (polycam_utils writes depth_file_path per frame) into transforms.json, then splatfacto (gsplat) trains.
all.license: Apache-2.0
all.weights: none
all.inputs: posed RGB (ARKit) plus optional LiDAR depth; tens to hundreds of frames
all.speed: splatfacto per-scene training in minutes on one GPU
all.gpu: single CUDA GPU
all.fit: Format reference only. Its transforms.json with depth_file_path is the common format that DN-Splatter and Brush read. Exporting our scanner bundle to it unlocks those tools for free comparison baselines on rung 1. We already run gsplat directly, so there's no need to adopt the framework, which hasn't been pushed since July 2025.
